newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MULDER GOAL GIVES SCHALKE UEFA SEMIFINAL PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MULDER GOAL GIVES SCHALKE UEFA SEMIFINAL PLACE.

text.p: Schalke, arriving in Spain with a two-goal advantage, did enough to earn a UEFA Cup semifinal place after taking an early lead through Youri Mulder in their quarter-final second leg with Valencia on Tuesday.
The 3-1 aggregate win, 1-1 on the night, gave some revenge to the German league over Valencia, who had opened their European campaign by knocking out Bayern Munich.
Schalke went ahead in the 18th minute of a poor game when a mix-up in midfield let Mulder through the middle of the Valencia defence, and he had no problem in beating goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta.
"The goal left us destroyed," Valencia's Patxi Ferreira said.
Needing four goals to win, Valencia found a faint glimmer of hope when Antonio Poyatos rose above the German defence to head home a cross from the right by Enrique Romero just before the break.
But despite enjoying superior possession in the second half, Valencia failed to break down a solid German defence.
The home side clearly missed the organisational skills and inspiration of Ariel Ortega, the Argentine midfielder who has revolutionised their Spanish league fortunes but is not eligible for the UEFA.

Jorge Valdano made a triple substitution in the 56th minute and the Valencia coach was nearly rewarded moments later when one of the new men, Goran Vlaovic, pounced on a loose ball only to see his shot saved by Schalke goalkeeper Jens Lehmann.
Valencia's best efforts from then on came from high balls, in particular a Ferreira header which went just wide after defenders and forwards at the near post had appeared to hold each other down.

A bad-tempered second half threatened to get out of control at some stages. Mulder, who played a superb game, was left with a bloodied nose after going for a high ball with Jose Ignacio Hurtado, who was booked for the challenge.
